description: Emulates through-zero FM: it reverses the direction of a ramp wave fed into it whenever a modulator crosses a threshold, and reflects that modulator about the threshold to drive the carrier's FM input

params.text: Sets the modulator voltage at which the carrier reverses, from -5V to 5V; the THRESH input is added to it and the total is held inside that range
Scales the ramp input, from -2 at full counter-clockwise through 0 at noon to 2 at full clockwise, inverting the ramp below 0; the panel's arc is marked -5 and +5 but the knob reaches only -2 and 2

ON puts the ramp output through a spike remover, a lowpass dropping from 20000Hz to 500Hz whenever the input ramp's own edge is found, and puts the sine output through a second one; OFF leaves both in
ENJ reverses the ramp's direction and shifts its phase to match, the more faithful through-zero sound; XWY inverts the whole ramp while the modulator is below the threshold, and works on any waveform

inputs.text: Adds to the input level knob at 0.4 per volt, the total held between -2 and 2
Adds to the threshold knob volt for volt, the total held between -5V and 5V
The modulator: the carrier reverses whenever this voltage crosses the threshold, and this is the signal reflected to CV OUT
The carrier ramp wave, rising or falling; aim for 10V peak to peak after IN LVL, which is what the phase shifter is built around

outputs.text: 10V while the modulator is at or above the threshold and 0V below it, which also makes the module a comparator; mixing it into the other outputs strengthens the fundamental
The modulator reflected about the threshold, so it turns back where it would have crossed; patch it to the carrier oscillator's FM input
The ramp output put through a quadratic sine shaper and scaled to three quarters
The phase-shifted ramp, held between -5V and 5V

notes: there is no oscillator here: patch a ramp wave to the ramp input and a modulator to CV IN, and take the ramp or sine output back out
every jack on the module reads or writes one channel, so a polyphonic cable is reduced to its first channel
the two lights show how far the modulator is from the threshold, the green one while it is above and the red one while it is below
keep THRESHOLD at noon for the steadiest behaviour, and run the carrier above the modulator in frequency for the strongest timbral effect
